newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks edge up to record close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks edge up to record close.

text.p: SPI futures cl 2546 +7 US 30yr (cl) 6.96 +0.06
10yrbond futs 92.290 -0.020 Gold NY 342.95 Lon fix 342.25
*Stocks ended a rangebound session firmer, the market finishing at a record closing high. Volume 400.8 million, value A$676.9 million, 1,112 stocks traded, 346 steady, 424 up, 342 down.
Australian stocks ended slightly firmer on Thursday, with the market range-bound for most of the session but traders finding enough motivation late in the day to lift shares to a record closing high.

The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed up 4.7 points at 2,547.9, eclipsing Wednesday's previous record close of 2,543.2 by 4.7 points. The market also touched an intra-day record high of 2,555.2, surpassing its previous record high of 2,543.5 which was also reached on Wednesday.
June share price index futures ended seven points up at 2,546, a thin 1.9 point discount to the underlying index.
"Apart from interest in some of the major banks it was a very quiet session," a Sydney-based dealer said.
The dealer said National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) and the ordinary and partly-paid stock of Commonwealth Bank of Australia were keenly sought.

"All the major banks have been sold down after half year results from Westpac (Banking Corp Ltd), ANZ (Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd) and NAB showed it would be difficult for them to continue to improve earnings," the dealer said.
Woodside Petroleum bounded 43 cents higher to A$11.279 after Wednesday's announcement of plans to set up a A$10 billion LNG processing plant in the Northern Territory.

Another oustanding issue was diamond explorer, Cluff Resources Pacific NL, whose shares jumped 3.3 cents to 6.5 cents on heavy turnover after it said it found 56 quality gems from its "Streak of Luck" mine in New South Wales.
Troubled food group Burns Philp & Co lost five cents to A$1.74 as investors remained disillusioned with its restructure plan announced on Monday.

Papua New Guinea resources group Orogen Minerals Ltd continued to perform strongly after the company's annual meeting in Port Moresby earlier this week. The stock climbed 21 cents to A$3.36 after adding 13 cents on Wednesday.

Media group News Corp fell seven cents to A$5.76 on trader's continuing concerns about its acquisitive American plans with sentiment further dampened by an Australian Financial Review article questioning Murdoch's U.S. satellite strategy.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about four to three with about a third of stocks traded remaining steady.
In other local markets, Australian debt futures ended the session groping for a clear direction after a mixed bag of wages data, coupled with comments by government and Treasury officials.
The yield on 10 year T-bonds closed at 7.68 percent, steady with Wednesday's levels.
The Australian dollar was clutching gains of close to a cent late Thursday after an explosive overseas rally took the top off a range that had held since early April.
By 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), the currency was trading at US$0.7825/30.
